title: s500-generic-44: Crossmodal face-name person-identity frequency tagging, SEEG of the left ventral temporal cortex (Volfart et al., 2020) (derivative)
description: Stereo-EEG (SEEG) recordings from the left ventral temporal cortex of patients with refractory epilepsy, collected during a crossmodal frequency-tagging paradigm. Faces and written names of a famous identity were presented at 4 Hz, with a different identity inserted every 7th item (0.571 Hz). Face-only and name-only control conditions were also run. The data are a derivative of the authors' low-pass filtered, epoched Letswave files, repackaged in BIDS (BrainVision format) for the three participants with non-empty data.
methods_description: SEEG was recorded with Micromed systems in patients at the University Hospital of Nancy during fast periodic visual stimulation (4 Hz, identity change every 7th item). The authors' Letswave 5 preprocessing applied a 30 Hz low-pass Butterworth filter (order 4) and cut each sequence from 2 s after onset to about 61 s. Sequences of the same condition were merged into one file, then converted to BrainVision with events and Talairach electrode coordinates.
